title: Workday CEO Aneel Bhusri: AI will displace ‘a lot’ of jobs within 5 years. Here’s who he says will be fine
source_used: Fortune (Fortune 500: Titans and Disruptors of Industry podcast transcript)
key_facts: Aneel Bhusri cofounded Workday in 2005 and returned as CEO in 2026; Workday has about 21,000 employees and about $10 billion in annual revenue.
Fortune's interviewer says about 60% of the Fortune 500 are Workday clients.
Bhusri on job displacement timeline: within the next five years.
He says agents will replace rote, repeatable work, citing a financial audit agent that will replace the work of junior auditors and a contract agent that replaces a subset of lawyers' work.
He says doers and individual contributors will be fine, and that people who learn to use AI tools will be in demand.
Workday joined RAISE US, a retraining effort started by former governors Gina Raimondo and Eric Holcomb, as an early investor.
He worries about an in-between period when jobs are displaced faster than people can be retrained.
quote_evidence: Timeline, I think it’s within the next five years.
The more rote, repeatable work that doesn’t require a lot of human judgment will be replaced by agents, and I think that’s already happening across the board.
If you’re a doer, an individual contributor, you’re going to be fine.
why_it_matters_hint: A CEO whose software serves most big US firms predicts quick displacement of routine white-collar work.
event_date: Interview published 15 Oct 2026; a May 2026 interview quote is referenced
notes: Podcast transcript, lightly edited by Fortune. Prediction is one executive’s opinion.
